column1: Basic, Standard, and Premium belong to Azure SQL Database's {{c1::DTU}} purchasing model.
column2:
These service tiers provide predefined resource bundles.
Review source

column1: Eligible SQL Server licenses can reduce General Purpose or Business Critical vCore costs through {{c1::Azure Hybrid Benefit}}.
column2:
Eligibility depends on the licensing and service configuration.
Review source

column1: The standard Business Critical architecture has one primary and {{c1::three secondary replicas}}.
column2:
The read scale-out secondary is included in this set.
Review source

column1: A Hyperscale database supports {{c1::zero to four}} high-availability secondary replicas.
column2:
Additional HA replicas provide ready failover targets at additional compute cost.
Review source

column1: Serverless compute scaling stays between the configured {{c1::minimum and maximum vCores}}.
column2:
The range also influences memory and I/O limits.
Review source

column1: Serverless compute is supported in General Purpose and {{c1::Hyperscale}}.
column2:
Business Critical does not support it, and Hyperscale auto-pause is in preview as of November 2026.
Review source

column1: The default MAXDOP for new Azure SQL databases since September 2020 is {{c1::8}}.
column2:
The change did not automatically modify older databases.
Review source

column1: To request serial query execution, set MAXDOP to {{c1::1}}.
column2:
This controls parallel execution, not how many queries can run concurrently.
Review source

column1: For one query, override database-level parallelism with {{c1::OPTION (MAXDOP 2)}} to request MAXDOP 2.
column2:
Place the hint on the SELECT statement.
Review source

column1: Set the current database's MAXDOP to 4 with {{c1::ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET MAXDOP = 4;}}
column2:
Insert FOR SECONDARY before SET to configure secondary-replica MAXDOP.
Review source

column1: Enable automatic index creation with {{c1::ALTER DATABASE CURRENT SET AUTOMATIC_TUNING (CREATE_INDEX = ON);}}
column2:
This configures index creation without explicitly changing the other automatic tuning options.
Review source

column1: As of November 2026, new Azure SQL databases default to compatibility level {{c1::170}}.
column2:
Existing databases retain their configured level unless someone changes it.
Review source

column1: Compatibility level 150 or higher allows {{c1::batch mode on rowstore}} for eligible queries without columnstore indexes.
column2:
Feature configuration and query-specific eligibility rules still apply.
Review source

column1: At level 150 or higher, {{c1::table variable deferred compilation}} uses the table variable's actual row count at first execution.
column2:
This replaces an initial fixed row-count guess.
Review source

column1: At level 150 or higher, {{c1::scalar UDF inlining}} turns eligible scalar functions into expressions within the calling query.
column2:
The function and calling query must meet the feature's eligibility rules.
Review source

column1: At level 160 or higher, {{c1::Parameter Sensitive Plan optimization}} handles parameterized queries that need different plans for different parameter values.
column2:
PSP avoids relying on one cached plan for all parameter values.
Review source

column1: At level 160 or higher, {{c1::cardinality estimation (CE) feedback}} improves estimation assumptions from repeated query execution.
column2:
The feature learns which estimation assumptions better fit the query and data.
Review source

column1: At level 170, {{c1::optional parameter plan optimization (OPPO)}} chooses plans based on whether an optional-filter parameter is NULL.
column2:
The feature applies to eligible optional-parameter query patterns.
Review source

column1: Set the current Azure SQL database's compatibility level to 170 with {{c1::ALTER DATABASE CURRENT SET COMPATIBILITY_LEVEL = 170;}}
column2:
Test the workload before changing production optimizer behavior.
Review source

column1: Enable database-scoped ad hoc plan stubs with {{c1::ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET OPTIMIZE_FOR_AD_HOC_WORKLOADS = ON;}}
column2:
This changes how first-time ad hoc batches are cached.
Review source
